Here is the itemized list of sources in footnotes and bibliography cited, relied upon, or disputed by J. Paul Tanner in "The New Covenant and Paul's Quotations from Hosea in Romans 9:25–26" (2005) that bear directly on the textual, hermeneutical, and covenantal problems of Romans 9:25–26 / Hosea 2:23 & 1:10 (B001-2 & B001-3) [1–52].
1. Sources Disputed by the Author
Alva J. McClain
Title: The Gospel of God's Grace
1
Year: 1973
1
Pages: Page 183
1
Why it matters: Disputed. Cited for claiming that the Hosea quotations in Romans 9:25–26 refer exclusively to the unbelief and future restoration of national Israel rather than Gentile inclusion—a view Tanner firmly rejects
1
.
John A. Battle, Jr.
Title: "Paul's Use of the Old Testament in Romans 9:25–26"
1
Year: 1981
1
Pages: Pages 115–129
1
Why it matters: Disputed. Cited for arguing that Romans 9:25–26 refers strictly to ethnic Israel rather than proving Gentile inclusion
1
.
David L. Turner
Title: "The Continuity of Scripture and Eschatology: Key Hermeneutical Issues"
1
Year: 1985
1
Pages: Pages 275–287 (specifically p. 281)
1
Why it matters: Disputed. Cited for contending (following Battle) that Paul in Romans 9:25–26 was thinking not of the church, but of the present unbelief and future restoration of ethnic Israel
1
.
Robert B. Chisholm Jr.
Title: "Hosea", in The Bible Knowledge Commentary, Old Testament, ed. John F. Walvoord and Roy B. Zuck
2
Year: 1985
2
Pages: Page 1386
2
Why it matters: Disputed. Cited for arguing that Paul quoted Hosea merely for an "analogy" or application of a principle to Gentiles rather than direct fulfillment
2
3
.
John A. Witmer
Title: "Romans", in The Bible Knowledge Commentary, New Testament, ed. John F. Walvoord and Roy B. Zuck
2
Year: 1983
2
Pages: Pages 478–479
2
Why it matters: Disputed. Cited for treating Paul's use of Hosea as a mere application of an analogical principle
2
3
.
S. Lewis Johnson
Title: "Evidence from Romans 9–11", in A Case for Premillennialism: A New Consensus, ed. Donald K. Campbell and Jeffrey L. Townsend
3
Year: 1992
3
Pages: Pages 199–223
3
Why it matters: Disputed. Cited for proposing an "analogical connection" between Israel and the church in Hosea, which Tanner (and Moo) rejects as hermeneutically inadequate to serve Paul's need for direct scriptural proof
3
.
Richard Daniels
Title: "How Does the Church Relate to the New Covenant? or, Whose New Covenant Is It, Anyway?"
4
Year: 1999
4
Pages: Pages 64–98 (specifically pp. 90, 92)
4
Why it matters: Disputed. Cited for his thesis that the church is merely a "nonparticipating mediator" of the New Covenant; Tanner insists Gentiles are full, direct participants in New Covenant spiritual blessings
4
.
Leon J. Wood
Title: "Hosea", in The Expositor's Bible Commentary, vol. 7
5
Year: 1985
5
Pages: Pages 178–180
5
Why it matters: Disputed. Cited for virtually ignoring the mention of "covenant" in Hosea 2:18 and failing to connect it to the New Covenant
5
.
Francis I. Andersen & David Noel Freedman
Title: Hosea (Anchor Bible)
5
Year: 1980
5
Pages: Page 281
5
Why it matters: Disputed. Cited for offering no help in identifying the covenant mentioned in Hosea 2:18
5
.
George Eldon Ladd
Title: "Historic Premillennialism", in The Meaning of the Millennium, ed. Robert G. Clouse
6
Year: 1977
6
Pages: Page 23
6
Why it matters: Disputed. Cited for claiming that the New Testament applies Old Testament prophecies to the church so as to identify the church as "spiritual Israel"—a supersessionist position Tanner explicitly refutes
6
7
.
2. Sources Relied Upon by the Author
W. Edward Glenny
Title: "The 'People of God' in Romans 9:25–26"
1
Year: 1995
1
Pages: Pages 42–59
1
Why it matters: Relied upon. Cited to support the conclusion that Paul uses Hosea 2:23 and 1:10 specifically to establish that God's "vessels of mercy" include Gentiles
1
.
Second Article: "The Israelite Imagery of 1 Peter 2", in Dispensationalism, Israel and the Church, ed. Craig A. Blaising and Darrell L. Bock (1992, pp. 156–187)
8
. Relied upon to show that Peter viewed Hosea 2:23 as a partial fulfillment with Gentile believers
8
9
.
Douglas J. Moo
Title: The Epistle to the Romans (NICNT)
1
unfold_less
3
10
11
Year: 1996
1
Pages: Pages 611, 612, 613
1
unfold_less
3
10
11
Why it matters: Relied upon in part / Disputed in part. Relied upon for textual analysis noting Paul intentionally altered Hosea's verb "I will say" to "I will call" (καλέσω) to match Romans 9:24
10
, and for demonstrating that mere "analogy" is hermeneutically insufficient for Paul
3
. Disputed regarding Moo's conclusion that OT predictions of renewed Israel find replacement fulfillment in the church
11
12
.
Walter C. Kaiser Jr.
Title: "An Assessment of 'Replacement Theology'"
13
Year: 1989
13
Pages: Pages 9–20
13
Why it matters: Relied upon. Cited for defining and assessing "replacement theology" (supersessionism) in biblical hermeneutics
13
14
.
Roy B. Zuck
Title: Basic Bible Interpretation
15
Year: 1991
15
Pages: Pages 267–269, 274–275
15
Why it matters: Relied upon. Cited for the hermeneutical concepts of "heightening" and references plenior (enlarging OT statements to fill them with related implications)
15
.
David K. Lowery
Title: "1 Corinthians", in The Bible Knowledge Commentary, New Testament
15
Year: 1983
15
Pages: Page 505
15
Why it matters: Relied upon. Cited for dating 1 Corinthians (ca. A.D. 54–55) to show Paul understood the church as one body by Spirit baptism prior to writing Romans
15
.
Rodney J. Decker
Title: "The Church's Relationship to the New Covenant"
4
Year: 1995
4
Pages: Pages 290–305
4
Why it matters: Relied upon. Cited for background on the church's relationship to the New Covenant
4
16
.
Larry D. Pettegrew
Title: The New Covenant Ministry of the Holy Spirit
17
18
Year: 1993
17
Pages: Pages 7–14, 27–45, 251–270, 268–269
17
18
Why it matters: Relied upon. Cited for the indwelling of the Holy Spirit as a New Covenant ministry enabling Gentiles to participate "in Christ"
17
18
.
Paul R. Thorsell
Title: "The Spirit in the Present Age: Preliminary Fulfillment of the Predicted New Covenant according to Paul"
19
Year: 1998
19
Pages: Pages 397–413
19
Why it matters: Relied upon. Cited for preliminary fulfillment of New Covenant Spirit promises in the present church age
19
.
Gary W. Light
Title: "The New Covenant in the Book of Hosea"
20
Year: 1993
20
Pages: Pages 219–238 (specifically p. 229)
20
Why it matters: Relied upon. Cited for demonstrating that Hosea 2:18 refers directly to the New Covenant through the marriage metaphor
20
.
Hans Walter Wolff
Title: Hosea (Hermeneia)
5
Year: 1974
5
Pages: Pages 51, 55
5
Why it matters: Relied upon. Cited for explicitly recognizing that Hosea 2:18 represents the first end-time reference to a "new covenant"
5
.
Andrew G. Shead
Title: "The Covenant and Pauline Hermeneutics", in The Gospel to the Nations, Perspectives on Paul's Mission, ed. Peter Bolt and Mark Thompson
21
Year: 2000
21
Pages: Pages 33–49
21
Why it matters: Relied upon. Cited for insight into Paul's understanding of New Covenant ministry in light of Jeremiah 31:31–34 and 2 Corinthians 3
21

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS This study has demonstrated that care must be taken in trying to understand and explain the apostolic understanding of the rela- tionship of Israel and the church. Ladd argued, "I do not see how it is possible to avoid the conclusion that the New Testament applies Old Testament prophecies to the New Testament church and in so doing identifies the church as spiritual Israel."22 Such a conclusion, however, fails to do justice to the New Testament. A better way of understanding the outworking of Old Testament national promises is to see them in light of the dawning comprehension of the New Covenant in the life of the early church as Gentiles were included. A study of Paul's use of Hosea 1-2 in Romans 9:25-26 illumines this very point.

Peter wrote that his audience (which surely included Gentiles) were "the people of God"—using words from Exodus 19:5-6 and Hosea 2:23. Peter was not merely applying a principle to his read- ers; he saw his readers as a partial fulfillment of these Old Testa- ment passages.9 This is not to say, however, that he regarded these verses as having complete fulfillment with Gentiles because Israel had forfeited her place of privilege before God. Instead Peter spoke of fulfillment, not merely application or analogy. So, while these Old Testament verses clearly pertained to Israel—to those physi- cally descended from Abraham—the promise need not be fulfilled with every physical descendant, and they had the potential to in- clude others who were not Jewish. This would not have been an- ticipated from an earlier point in salvation history, but it had be- come apparent in the days of the first century.

The more important issue, of course, is how Paul came to have his understanding about Hosea 1-2. It may be that this under- standing was contemporaneous with the revelation of the mystery mentioned in Ephesians 3. On the other hand several key devel- opments would have at least paved the way for Paul's insights into Hosea, and these are related to the progressive understanding about the New Covenant itself.12 Although the apostles did not grasp the full significance of Je- sus' statement, His announcement about the New Covenant on the eve of His crucifixion would certainly have been important to their understanding later. "And in the same way He took the cup after they had eaten, saying, This cup which is poured out for you is the new covenant in My blood' " (Luke 22:20). Thus they would have realized that the prophesied New Covenant of the Old Testament had arrived and was in operation (though not completely ful- filled).13 They were no longer participants in the Old Covenant with its rituals and sacrifices. A closer examination of the context of Hosea 2:23 reveals that the New Covenant is in view.17 Verse 18 states, "In that day I will also make a covenant for them." Although this verse says "a cove- nant," not "new covenant," the New Covenant is undoubtedly in l b Gentiles were participating in the New Covenant because they were "in Christ," and this had been made possible by Spirit baptism (see Pettegrew, The New Cove- nant Ministry of the Holy Spirit, 268-69). To say that Gentiles were participating in the New Covenant, however, does not mean that all Old Testament promises and expectations associated with the New Covenant would be realized by believing Gen- tiles. A careful reading of Jeremiah 30-31 and Ezekiel 36-37 (both of which are imbued with New Covenant thought) finds many prophetic details that can be ful- filled only with ethnic Israel in conjunction with Christ's return. In the midst of this experience the nation will plead with God and confess her sinfulness (31:18-19), and as a result the Lord will save (i.e., deliver) her from it (30:7). Following this national deliverance the Lord will regather Israel back to the land originally promised to Abraham (30:3; 31:8, 10; Ezek. 36:24; 37:21). This cannot be a spiritualized land, because Ezekiel clarifies that it is the land "in which your fathers lived" (37:25; cf. 36:28). Also agri- cultural blessings are included (36:29-30, 33-35). And the Lord will cleanse Israel of all her spiritual unfaithfulness (w. 25, 29, 33; 37:23), and the surviving remnant will enjoy His blessings (Jer. 31:12).

For example Israel must pass through "the time of Jacob's distress" (Jer. 30:7)—a probable reference to the "Great Tribulation"—in which the Lord will "chasten [her] justly" (v. 11)—an event slated for "the latter days" (v. 24). In the midst of this experience the nation will plead with God and confess her sinfulness (31:18-19), and as a result the Lord will save (i.e., deliver) her from it (30:7). Following this national deliverance the Lord will regather Israel back to the land originally promised to Abraham (30:3; 31:8, 10; Ezek. 36:24; 37:21). This cannot be a spiritualized land, because Ezekiel clarifies that it is the land "in which your fathers lived" (37:25; cf. 36:28). Also agri- cultural blessings are included (36:29-30, 33-35). And the Lord will cleanse Israel of all her spiritual unfaithfulness (w. 25, 29, 33; 37:23), and the surviving remnant will enjoy His blessings (Jer. 31:12).
